race_context: How the seat is elected: one prosecuting attorney is elected for each judicial circuit to a four-year term, with no term limit, and every candidate must be a lawyer admitted to practice in Indiana {ic_3_10_2_12}{clark_pros}{in_guide}.

Finding the current prosecutor and the office's work: county prosecutor websites describe the office's divisions, such as criminal and child support, and the Indiana Prosecuting Attorneys Council directs people with case-specific questions to their local county prosecutor {clark_pros}{ipac}.

Following the office's budget: the county council appropriates money each year for deputy prosecutors, investigators, staff and office expenses beyond the state-paid salaries, so county council budget hearings and minutes show how the office is funded {ic_33_39_6_2}.

Comparing candidates: the Indiana Election Division publishes the official list of candidates on the November 3, 2026 ballot; this year voters will also decide Public Question 1 on bail, an issue prosecutors argue in court {in_list}{indypolitics_2026_bail}.
